summary: Rapid 5xx elevation during accept-queue flush and ephemeral hotplug causing upstream runtime crashes
description:
Issue summary: Customers began reporting sudden elevated 5xx rates for streaming and short-payload routes starting 2026-03-13 12:20 UTC. Errors manifest as API Gateway 502/503 and a correlated spike in upstream runtime exits on nodes handling ephemeral hotplug of model variants.

Impact: Customer-facing generated-text requests for several dedicated tenants (including IterateAI) experienced ~18% error rate spikes for ~35 minutes, impacting SLAs. Some long-lived streaming sessions saw half-complete responses and client reconnect storms.

Environment: prod us-east-1; dedicated pool for IterateAI; mixed embed+chat traffic; models: redwood-rlhf-v1 + open-chat-7b variant fanout enabled.

Observed behavior:
- API Gateway returned 502/503 on short requests and streaming routes.
- Upstream runtime logs show NVML driver reset traces coincident with model hotplug events.
- Accept queue length grew rapidly (~X10 baseline) then flushed as the ephemeral scheduler moved variants between workers.
- Keepalive reaper observed many half-open HTTP/2 sessions and aggressively closed them, amplifying connection churn.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Trigger controlled hotplug of a model variant across an ephemeral pool (canary -> all).
2) Simultaneously ramp a mix of short chat and embedding requests at 2x normal concurrency.
3) Observe accept queue growth and increased hedged retries from clients.

Initial logs/metrics snippets:
- apigw: "accept_queue_len=1250 -> flush -> 502 downstream-unavailable"
- runtime: "nvml: GPU reset detected; exiting process (signal 6)"
- proxy: "http2: half-closed stream count spike; keepalive_reaper evicted 430 sockets"

Notes: This looks like a multi-component coupling failure: ephemeral hotplug caused momentary backpressure on the serving runtime (GPU driver resets when multiple model variants load), the accept queue in APIGW accumulated connections, and the keepalive/eviction logic collapsed many long-poll connections which triggered client retry storms and hedged retries that amplified the upstream overload.
investigation_notes:
Timeline:
- 12:18 UTC: deployment orchestration initiated variant swap across ephemeral pool.
- 12:20 UTC: accept queue length begins to grow; apigw latency P50->P95 jumps.
- 12:22 UTC: first NVML reset observed on runtime-node-12; runtime restarted and reclaimed but model reload contention continues.
- 12:24 UTC: apigw keepalive eviction increases; downstream healthchecks report transient failures.

What we've checked:
- Kernel/GPU driver versions (NVML) match supported list but there is a known intermittent reset under concurrent hotplug on older drivers; hardware vendor has a bulletin.
- Traces link client hedged retries to the moment accept queue flushed; retry amplification pattern matches previous incidents but root cause is different (hotplug timing).
- Heap / GPU memory fragmentation examined: fragmentation increases after repeated hotplug cycles; look for memory leak in the serving-runtime loader.

Hypotheses:
1) Concurrent model hotplug + prefetch causes GPU driver to reset on certain cards -> runtime process exits, leaving apigw with unhealthy upstreams -> 502s.
2) Accept queue flush combined with keepalive reaper mis-tuning turns a small overload into a retry stampede.

Evidence:
- NVML traces and stack dumps attached in internal artifact (see PR).
- Grafana: AcceptQueueGrow dashboard shows correlated spikes with runtime restarts.

Next investigative steps:
- Reproduce in staging with controlled hotplug pace and increased telemetry on NVML calls.
- Run a driver-level stress test per vendor guidance.
- Audit keepalive reaper threshold and hedged retry backoff in APIGW config.
- Capture core dumps from runtime on NVML reset for memory allocator inspection.

resolution:
Mitigation applied:
- Paused variant hotplug rollout and reduced concurrency of model prefetching in the dedicated pool.
- Increased APIGW keepalive threshold and backoff to prevent immediate eviction-induced retry storms.
- Disabled client-side hedged retries for affected routes temporarily.
- Merged runtime fix to serialize hotplug/model-loads (PR 2487).

Permanent fix & follow-ups:
- Schedule GPU firmware update per vendor bulletin across affected nodes (SRE action).
- Add guard in runtime to detect pending NVML-reset sequence and fail fast before heavy prefetch.
- Tune accept-queue and keepalive reaper interplay: create a small circuit-breaker to reject new accepts when upstream health degrades to avoid retry amplification.
- Postmortem to be published to Confluence (link will be added).

Status: Mitigations in place; canary showing stable behavior. Customer notified of workaround and timeline for firmware rollout. Follow-up items opened in engineering backlog.
